overview: Rise 6.1.30's Speed module is a thin dispatcher: fifteen mode classes under module.impl.movement.speed, each listening on StrafeEvent (some also on PacketReceiveEvent), a default of Vanilla, and a TeleportEvent listener that can disable the module. The modes share MoveUtil's write-through strafe: event.setSpeed pins the horizontal magnitude the movement system applies to motion, so the C03 stream carries the boosted positions while the packet rate stays one per tick. The default VanillaSpeed jumps every ground tick and pins speed 1.0 blocks per tick; NCPSpeed is the flagship, with jumpMotion 0.4 (0.4-0.42), groundSpeed 1.75 times the 0.2873 sprint base (about 0.50 blocks per tick), a bunnySlope 0.66 decay, a timer multiplier up to 10, an S12 velocity damage boost and low-hop and y-port motionY resets of -0.098. onDisable restores timerSpeed to 1 and optionally stops the player.

sections.p: Speed.java owns the mode value (Vanilla, Strafe, Interact, Vulcan, Watchdog, NCP, Funcraft, Verus, BlocksMC, MineMenClub, KoksCraft, Legit, Intave, Sparky, Grim), the disableOnTeleport and stopOnDisable booleans, the onDisable that resets mc.timer.timerSpeed and optionally calls MoveUtil.stop(), and the teleport listener that toggles the module off when the server teleports it. All actual movement logic lives in the mode classes, each a Mode<Speed> with its own listeners, so the dispatcher itself is inert and the mode selection determines the entire packet-level behavior.

VanillaSpeed jumps on every ground tick while moving and pins the horizontal speed to 1.0, the whole mode in one listener. NCPSpeed is the reference implementation: the packet listener captures S12PacketEntityVelocity for the player and stores the knockback magnitude as speed when the boost setting is on; the StrafeEvent listener switches on offGroundTicks, setting motionY to MoveUtil.jumpBoostMotion(jumpMotion) (0.42 when collided horizontally) and speed to base times groundSpeed on the ground tick, applying speed -= bunnySlope * (speed - base) at tick 1, and speed -= speed / BUNNY_FRICTION (159.9) afterwards; the timer setting scales timerSpeed while moving and resets to 1 when the player stops; lowHop resets motionY to -0.09800000190734864 at offGroundTicks 4 and yPort does the same at tick 5 when the current motionY is within 0.12 of it; hurtBoost substitutes a boostSpeed magnitude while ticksSincePlayerVelocity is inside hurTime; colliding horizontally resets speed to base; and the event closes with setSpeed(max(speed, base), Math.random() / 2000), a sub-epsilon jitter on the magnitude. The TeleportEvent listener and onDisable zero the speed field.

MoveUtil.getAllowedHorizontalDistance computes the NCP-style allowed distance the modes multiply: WALK_SPEED 0.221, times MOD_SPRINTING 1.3 when sprinting (0.2873), times the sneak 0.3, web, swim, ice and depth-strider modifiers, times 1 + 0.2 * amplifier for speed potions, or a fixed 0.29 under slowness. MoveUtil.setSpeed maps the magnitude onto the movement direction and writes motionX and motionZ directly, so the next C03 position reflects the pinned speed and vanilla friction is bypassed; the write-through happens per tick, so the C03 rate never changes and the fingerprint is purely horizontal magnitude, not packet rate.

files.label: Speed.java
files.explanation: The dispatcher: the fifteen-mode ModeValue with Vanilla as default, the disableOnTeleport and stopOnDisable settings, the onDisable timerSpeed reset, and the teleport listener. It shows the module surface but no movement math, which is why the mode file below matters for the analysis.

files.label: NCPSpeed.java (flagship mode)
files.explanation: The mode that defines the module's real behavior: the S12 velocity boost listener, the per-offGroundTicks speed schedule (groundSpeed 1.75 times base on the ground tick, bunnySlope decay at tick 1, BUNNY_FRICTION decay afterwards), the timer multiplier, the lowHop and yPort motionY resets, and the final setSpeed with sub-epsilon jitter. Its default settings produce the 0.50 blocks-per-tick horizontal pin that the countering checks measure.

countering.label: NCP SurvivalFly (horizontal speed envelope)
countering.explanation: There is no moving/player/Speed.java in this NCP tree, so the horizontal speed check lives inside SurvivalFly: check() derives the allowed distance from prepareSpeedEstimation (sprint acceleration plus 30% for 1.8), estimateNextSpeed predicts the per-tick distance, and handlePredictableMove computes offset = hDistance - hAllowedDistance, with the violation (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 and a set-back. The predicted sprint distance is about 0.28-0.31 blocks per tick, so NCPSpeed's pinned 0.50 gives an offset near 0.19 and a violation around 19 on the first move, and VanillaSpeed's 1.0 gives roughly 0.69 over, around 69. The vertical side is not the tell: the jump itself is credited through the jump envelope and arms the 10-tick jumpDelay window, and the low-hop and y-port -0.098 resets are inside the envelope, so the horizontal pin is what every mode exposes.

countering.label: Arc v2 Speed (moving magnitude)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Speed uses the same 0.2873 base (getBaseMoveSpeed, the 1.3 sprint multiplier over walk speed) and stages its expectations by state. On the ground the expected value is thisMove / groundTime + base with groundTime capped at 8, and once groundTicks reaches 5 a sustained speed above expected flags under the onground_expected branch: 0.50 against 0.50/8 + 0.2873 = 0.3498 keeps the flag after five grounded ticks. Off the ground the expected value is base plus a stage keyed on vertical motion (0.049 at zero vertical, 0.08 below 0.34, 0.3261 above), so 0.50 passes the rising ticks (expected 0.6134 at vertical >= 0.34) but flags every descending tick against 0.2873 + 0.08 = 0.3673 under the BunnyHop label, giving about two ticks of ascent grace before the descent flags accumulate. The setback location is stored from the last clean move, so the player is snapped back to the last legal position.

countering.label: Hawk Speed (momentum conservation)
countering.explanation: Hawk's Speed check conserves momentum: expected = friction * lastSpeed * handleMultipliers + (maxForce + handleAdders + EPSILON), where friction comes from the block slipperiness on ground (0.91 in air) and the adders include the vanilla sprint-jump boost of +0.2 when sprinting and jumping. The discrepancy (currentSpeed - expected) accumulates per player across moves, and the check flags when the total passes DISCREPANCY_THRESHOLD (default 0.1), with the violation scaled by discrepancy * 10. With a pinned 0.50 and ground friction 0.6 the expected value lands near 0.33, so one ground tick contributes around 0.17 of discrepancy and the first updatePos move flags; the Strafe ratchet of the NCP mode makes it worse. The jump adder only forgives the vanilla 0.2 sprint-jump boost, never a magnitude pinned above it, and the S12 damage boost feeds a knockback-derived speed the adders never account for. The sub-epsilon jitter on setSpeed is below the model's resolution, so it does not mask the magnitude.
